layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We present TopoMortar, a brick wall dataset that is the first dataset specifically de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: signed to evaluate topology-focused image segmentation methods, such as topology loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: functions. Motivated by the known sensitivity of methods to dataset challenges, such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as small training sets, noisy labels, and out-of-distribution test-set images, TopoMor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tar is created to enable in two ways investigating methods’ effectiveness at improving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology accuracy. First, by eliminating dataset challenges that, as we show, impact

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the effectiveness of topology loss functions. Second, by allowing to represent different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset challenges in the same dataset, isolating methods' performance from dataset chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenges. TopoMortar includes three types of labels (accurate, pseudo-labels, and noisy la-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: bels), two fixed training sets (large and small), and in-distribution and out-of-distribution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test-set images. We compared eight loss functions on TopoMortar, and we found that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clDice achieved the most topologically accurate segmentations, and that the relative ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vantageousness of the other loss functions depends on the experimental setting. Addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tionally, we show that data augmentation and self-distillation can elevate Cross entropy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice loss to surpass most topology loss functions, and that those simple methods can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enhance topology loss functions as well. TopoMortar and our code can be found at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: https://jmlipman.github.io/TopoMortar.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Deep learning has demonstrated extraordinary potential for image segmentation, yet even

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state-of-the-art models [6] cannot guarantee the connectivity of thin tubular structures, such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as axons, vessels, and fibers. As a result, minor misclassifications can break the continuity of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these structures, compromising their subsequent quantification. Topology loss functions []

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aim to address this issue by encouraging models to produce segmentations with the correct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: number of topological structures, such as connected components, holes, and hollows. How-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever, their effectiveness is not completely well understood due to limitations in the datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used to evaluate them.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Topology loss functions have been evaluated on datasets with regions requiring precise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connectivity, such as blood vessels. Datasets, in addition to their high-level segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: task (e.g., segmenting blood vessels on fundus retina images), present challenges that are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rarely discussed or accounted for, such as class imbalance, small dataset size, noisy labels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo-labels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and dataset challenges obscures under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: standing when and where topology loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: functions improve topology accuracy. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instance, a method addressing the same

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenge across different datasets (e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice loss in class-imbalanced datasets) may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increase topology accuracy simply because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ular challenge; however, it will not improve

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yet been evaluated on a dataset without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges (e.g., class imbalance, imperfect

layout_dets.text: the possibilities for methods to increase topology accuracy by tackling dataset challenges.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Thus, an increase in topology accuracy can be attributed to the method's capability to learn

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the data's topological properties. It is also unknown whether simple methods addressing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset challenges, such as data augmentation and self-distillation, are more effective than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology losses, and whether topology loss functions can be further improved with such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods. Our main contributions are:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We release the first dataset specifically acquired to investigate whether topology-focused

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods improve topology accuracy and effectively learn data's topological properties.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We compare extensively, with 10 random seeds and statistical significance tests, Cross

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entropy Dice loss with six topology and one non-topology loss functions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We show that clDice was the only evaluated topology loss function that improved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology accuracy in most of the experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • We demonstrate that data augmentation and self-distillation can increase topology ac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curacy even when optimizing topology loss functions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Topology loss functions have been evaluated on many different image segmentation datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where topology accuracy has been considered essential. The most used datasets across 28

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a dataset of fundus retina images for blood vessel segmentation that has 20 training and 20

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test images. The Massachusetts Roads dataset [B4] consists of 1171 aerial images for road

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation split into 1108, 14, and 49 training, validation, and test set images. The CREMI

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset1 is comprised of three 3D electron-microscopy images of the brain tissue of adult

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Drosophila melanogaster. Other datasets used to evaluate loss functions are CrackTree []

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (photographs of concrete cracks); ISBI12 [] and ISBI13 [] (electron-microscopy images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of neurons); RoadTracer [] and DeepGlobe [] (aerial images of roads); and ACDC [0]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and left ventricle UK biobank [B9] (cardiac magnetic resonance images).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These datasets present different challenges, making it difficult to determine whether im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proved topology accuracy stems from a method's suitability to dataset challenges, its suit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ability to a specific task, or its effective learning of the data's topological properties. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DRIVE dataset is extremely small; around one-third of the training set images of the Mas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sachusetts Roads dataset are corrupted (see Appendix A); The CREMI dataset only provides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the instance segmentation of the neurons, thus, each study had to derive its own neuron bor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ders pseudo-labels—a process that has not been documented and has been likely carried out

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differently (see Appendix B); CrackTree's labels are one-pixel width lines (i.e., noisy labels,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: see Appendix C). On DRIVE—the most used dataset—previous studies have conducted 5-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fold cross-validation on the 20 training set images [5], 3-fold cross-validation on 30 images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [4]], 3-fold cross-validation on the 20 training set images [], ], applied a 16-4-20 train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing, validation, and test set split [, , 43], a 16-4 train-test split [29], or an unspecified split

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the 20 training set images [, ]. This inconsistency is likely due to a combination of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: factors, including its small size, the lack of a fixed train-validation split, and the unavailabil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity of the test-set labels. More details on the datasets and experimental discrepancies across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: studies can be found in Appendix D.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 TopoMortar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our dataset, TopoMortar, is a brick wall dataset consisting of 420 RGB images of 512 ×

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 512 pixels for the task of mortar segmentation. We have chosen brick walls with mortar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because of the well-defined topological properties of the bricks and mortar. The mortar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: allows variation in the labels, and the brick walls are well suited for testing specific shifts

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in domain such as occluding objects, color change, etc. TopoMortar's task (i.e., mortar

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation in red brick walls) is relatively simple by design; in contrast to existing datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that are more complex, an improvement in topology accuracy in TopoMortar is less likely to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be due to a more suitable choice of the neural network, optimizer, training time, etc.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TopoMortar is built to address previous dataset limitations and to avoid discrepancies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the experimental settings of future studies. To this end, TopoMortar includes 1) a fixed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training-validation-test set split (50-20-350), 2) two fixed training sets (50 and 10), 3) accu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rate, noisy, and pseudo-labels for the training and validation sets, 4) the manual annotations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of all the images, and 5) several OOD test set images (85% of the test set) divided into six

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: groups portraying different challenges (see fig. 1 (top)). The training and validation sets con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tain images that align with the general concept of a red brick wall, i.e., reddish bricks with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mortar horizontally and vertically oriented and without any shadows or objects. The test

layout_dets.text: set images are divided into seven groups: in-distribution brick walls that are similar to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previous related studies (Appendix D). Moreover, as our experiments demonstrate, its large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training set consisting of 50 images suffices to achieve significantly higher topology accu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: racy than the small training set of only 10 images, allowing to study whether topology losses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: advantageousness decreases when increasing the training set size.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TopoMortar allows to investigate whether methods are effective at improving topol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ogy accuracy in two ways. First, by eliminating dataset challenges (i.e., confounding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: factors such as scarce training data, inaccurate labels, and OOD test-set images) with Topo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mortar's large training set, accurate labels, and ID test set. Without dataset challenges, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method has limited ability to exploit specific dataset characteristics to increase accuracy and,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore, topology accuracy. Thus, an improvement in topology accuracy can be attributed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to the effective learning of topological properties. Second, by permitting to assess, on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same dataset, model robustness against various dataset challenges: scarce training data,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pseudo-labels, noisy labels, and OOD test-set images. By utilizing the same training set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images (thus, fixing the dataset-related effects), an increase in topology accuracy across all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges indicates the learning of topology information. More details about TopoMortar,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its labels, and its suitability for assessing topology accuracy can be found in Appendix E.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4 Experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We conducted four sets of experiments. First, we investigated the impact of dataset chal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lenges and limitations on the effectiveness of topology loss functions in datasets used by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: previous work. Second, we compared topology loss functions on TopoMortar in a setup

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without dataset challenges. Third, we compared topology loss functions across different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset challenges. Fourth, we studied the extent to which two simple methods for tackling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset challenges that do not directly aim at increasing topology accuracy (data augmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion and self-distillation) can actually increase topology accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We compared Cross entropy and Dice loss (CEDice), RegionWise loss [], TopoLoss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: []], TOPO [B6], Warping loss [[2], clDice [[4], Skeleton Recal1 [25], and cbDice [3].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: More details about the loss functions can be found in Appendix F. In addition to computing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice coefficient [3] and Hausdorff distance (95th percentile) [], we computed the Betti

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: errors. The Betti 0 error

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refers to the difference in the number of connected components,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while the Betti 1 error

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refers to the difference in the number of holes (in most cases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corresponding to the bricks in TopoMortar).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All our experiments were run with 10 different random seeds, providing us with suffi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cient measurements to evaluate the significance of performance differences. For this, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: computed paired permutation tests with 10,000 random iterations. We trained nnUNet for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 12,000 iterations on batches of 10 images with deep supervision [] and stochastic gradient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: descent, with a learning rate of 0.01, nesterov momentum of 0.99, weight decay of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and polynomial learning rate decay

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . We employed 10 data augmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformations (see Appendix G). We implemented our experiments in MONAI [] and Py-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Torch [B8], and we ran our experiments in two clusters with several Tesla A100, V100, A10,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and A40, ranging from 16 to 40 GB of GPU memory.

layout_dets.text: 4.4 Topology losses with data augmentation and self-distillation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We studied the impact on topology accuracy of two simple methods for tackling dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges. First, we accounted for the presence of OOD images with a simple data aug-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation method that increased the colors' diversity in the images and that we applied with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a probability of 50%. This data augmentation, which we refer to as RandHue, converted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the images to the HSV color space; randomly chose the same hue for all pixels; randomly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shifted the saturation and value; and converted the image back to RGB (see examples in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Appendix M). Second, we accounted for labels being pseudo-labels and noisy labels by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training with self-distillation [9]a strategy known to be advantageous with those types

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of labels. We employed self-distillation due to its simplicity and because it incorporated no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extra hyper-parameters. To keep the total iterations to 12,000 as in all our experiments, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained the models for 4,000 iterations, generated soft labels for the training set, trained on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those labels for another 4,000 iterations, and repeated the process one more time.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The segmentations and, particularly, their topology accuracy were generally better than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in the previous experiment where no dataset challenge was directly tackled. clDice also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieved the best segmentations in most cases, and Skeleton Recall also outperformed in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the presence of noisy labels. As in the previous experiment, the second-best topology loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: function depended on the specific experimental setup. Applying RandHue improved the Dice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coefficients in the OOD images and decreased the Betti errors significantly in both the ID and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: OOD test set (Table 2 vs. Table 3 (top-right)). The decrease in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: error occurred across

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all OOD groups, whereas the decrease in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: error occurred only in “angles", “colors",

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and “shadows" (see Appendix N). When training on pseudo-labels and noisy labels, self-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distillation improved Dice coefficients and topology accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We presented TopoMortar, a dataset specifically created to study the effectiveness of topology-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: focused image segmentation methods. We showed that existing datasets exhibit challenges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that were not previously considered and that influence topology accuracy. We compared

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: eight loss functions on TopoMortar on a setup without dataset challenges and then studied

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model robustness in the presence of those challenges. Finally, we investigated the extent to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which simple data augmentation and self-distillation can increase topology accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluated topology loss functions on different datasets, following the standard exper-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imental approach. Additionally, we tackled the challenges of data scarcity and noisy labels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in DRIVE and CrackTree datasets with a larger dataset and with a method to learn from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noisy labels, respectively. Our experiments revealed two key points. First, no topology loss

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: VALVERDE ET AL.: TOPOMORTAR

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: function was the best across all settings, which contrasts with topology loss function studies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where the proposed loss function always outperforms the others. Second, by tackling dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: challenges, not only topology accuracy improves but also the relative advantageousness of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the topology loss functions changes. Importantly, this experiment does not reveal when and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: why specific topology loss functions are advantageous, as comparing across datasets entan-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gles dataset tasks and dataset challenges. For instance, cbDice and Warping loss achieved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher topology accuracy than CEDice in the DRIVE dataset while, on CrackTree, they did

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not surpass CEDice. This may indicate that cbDice and Warping loss lead to models robust

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: against scarce training data but not against noisy labels; or that cbDice and Warping loss are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly well suited for blood vessel segmentation; or both.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluated the topology loss functions on TopoMortar eliminating dataset challenges

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by ensuring sufficient training data, training time, accurate labels, ID test-set images, strong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: data augmentation, and a state-of-the-art deep learning model. This scenario was either as-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sumed or not discussed in previous works. In this challenging setup, only clDice and Skele-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ton Recall achieved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: errors smaller and significantly different than CEDice, with clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also achieving smaller and significantly different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: errors, demonstrating the potential of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: skeletonization-based topology loss functions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We investigated model robustness against dataset challenges after optimizing topol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ogy loss functions on TopoMortar. In contrast to experiments on other datasets, TopoMor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tar allows fixing the dataset task (i.e., segmenting mortar in red brick walls), permitting to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: study the effect of each dataset challenge, individually, on the potential advantageousness of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology losses. We observed 1) that clDice was generally the best-performing loss, 2) that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Skeleton Recall worked best specifically under the presence of noisy labels, and 3) that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance of the other losses varied depending on the dataset challenge. These results,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in line with the other experiments, indicate that clDice is truly effective at enhancing topol-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ogy accuracy. The outperformance of Skeleton Recall over clDice on noisy labels can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: explained by its emphasis on the foreground region (true positives, false negatives), as, on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TopoMortar's noisy labels, the foreground corresponds to a thicker and more accurate skele-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ton than what clDice produces. Thus, it may be that with a different type of noisy labels []

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Skeleton Recall performs differently.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We also studied the impact of data augmentation and self-distillation on topology accu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: racy. These simple and well-established strategies improved the baseline CEDice when train-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing on a large training set with accurate labels and when optimizing on noisy and pseudo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labels (Tables 2 and 3), making CEDice outperform the majority of topology loss functions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Although it is unsurprising that data augmentation, self-distillation, and other methods []

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve performance, limited research has investigated to what extent they can increase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology accuracy, or even if they can make standard models trained on CEDice surpass

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology loss functions. Considering that topology loss functions are generally computa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tionally expensive CPU- and GPU-wise (Appendix O), our results demonstrate that focusing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on improving regular accuracy by utilizing methods that account for dataset challenges can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be a resource-friendly alternative to topology loss functions to increase topology accuracy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Moreover, combining such methods with topology loss functions further improved topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy in most cases, especially in the OOD test-set images (Table 3).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TopoMortar was designed to be simple to prevent methods from exploiting dataset partic-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ularities to increase topology accuracy. Despite mortar's relatively simple topology, topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: accuracy on TopoMortar has a very high correlation with the topology accuracy on CREMI,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DRIVE, FIVES, and CrackTree datasets (Appendix P), demonstrating the generalizability

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of results across biological, non-biological datasets, and structures with different topology.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: VALVERDE ET AL.: TOPOMORTAR

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6 Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Previous benchmarks on existing datasets have not allowed to completely understand whether

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods improve topology accuracy merely by focusing on the dataset characteristics (thus,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disregarding topology), or by learning data's topological properties. In contrast, our Topo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mortar dataset permits to study this research question by eliminating confounding factors and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by enabling the investigation of model robustness against various dataset challenges. clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generally achieved the most topologically accurate segmentations while Skeleton Recall per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: formed best on noisy labels. Additionally, data augmentation and self-distillation helped in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improving topology accuracy, even when employed jointly with topology loss functions.
